title: More reasoning effort, no answer
note: Mercury 3 at `high` spent the whole 32,768-token budget on hidden reasoning and returned nothing. The same problem is solved 5 of 5 times at `low` (6–12k tokens, 13–22 s) and at `instant`, but 0 of 10 times at `medium` and `high`. Raising the cap to 131,072 (R1b) rescued 1 of 6 such calls. Claude Haiku, Gemini, GPT-6 Luna `medium` and gpt-oss `medium` solve it 5 of 5.

title: An ill-posed easy problem: the others guess, Mercury 3 keeps thinking
note: The task says 'find the directrix of a parabola', but its one example (5, 3, 2 → −198) matches no textbook formula; the hidden reference uses an unusual one. Most AR arms write the standard formula and fail the tests (Claude Haiku `medium` reverse-engineers the example and passes 5 of 5). Mercury 3 reasons until the cap on all 10 samples at `medium` and `high`, and on 4 of 5 at `low`, apparently trying to reconcile the example with the math. Same score as a wrong guess, but ~32k tokens and close to a minute per call.

title: At `instant`, the runaway happens in plain sight
note: With no hidden reasoning at `instant`, Mercury 3 reasons in the visible answer instead. On this hard LiveCodeBench problem it wrote ~138,000 characters of analysis ('Key observation… Instead, we can think in terms of…') and hit the cap before writing any code. 17 of 3,185 `instant` calls ended this way; no AR arm had a single one.

title: A repetition loop inside a code literal
note: Asked to find adverbs in a sentence, Mercury 3 started a hard-coded list of adverbs and never closed it: ~110,000 characters of words, many repeated ('apparently' and 'seemingly' recur), until the cap. The code fence never closed, so the grader saw a syntax error. Degenerate repetition isn't specific to diffusion, but in R2 only Mercury 3 `instant` ever hit the cap while writing visible text.

title: In the agent loop: one answer expected, many found
note: Asked which driver set a 0:01:27 lap in race 161, Mercury 3 `instant` found that the hint's pattern (`time LIKE '1:27%'`) matches 82 laps by several drivers (the tool showed the first 50), and that an exact `= '1:27'` match returns nothing. Expecting a single player, it kept reasoning in visible text in turn 6 ('Let me reconsider…', 93 times) until the 32,768-token cap: ~127,000 characters, and 54 s for the task. 31 of 2,976 Mercury 3 `instant`/`low` tasks ended in a budget-out turn; no AR arm had any.

title: The right answer, written as prose instead of a tool call
note: gpt-oss on Cerebras found the right query (it returns exactly the gold rows), then replied with it as JSON text instead of calling `submit_answer`, twice, ignoring the nudge to use a tool, and ran out of turns. It is the fastest model per call, but behaviour like this (773 malformed tasks at `low`, 14.3% turn cap) is why its per-call lead mostly disappears per task.

title: Exploring one table at a time until the turns run out
note: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite spends turns on schema exploration (four `describe_table` calls in separate turns, plus a `PRAGMA table_list` the read-only sandbox refuses). It reaches the right query in turn 7, re-runs a variant in turn 8, and hits the 8-turn cap without submitting. It hit the cap on 28.8% of tasks, the most of any arm, which is why its 0.63 s calls become a 4.4 s task.

title: Strict JSON with leaked tool-call markup
note: Under strict `response_format: json_schema`, Mercury 3 produced the right JSON object and then appended `</|inc_tool_call_ml|parameter>`, which looks like its internal tool-call template. Of its 6 violations, 4 end in this marker, 1 in a bare `</`, and 1 was empty. Every other arm had zero. A structured-output gap that appears only when tools are also offered.

title: The AR counterpart: confident, fast, and never looked
note: With a JSON schema set, Claude Haiku answered all 150 tasks in the first turn without calling a single tool, writing SQL from the question and hint alone. Here the guessed query returns the wrong rows. The schema was always valid; the exploration never happened: 53.3% EX versus 58.9% in tool mode.
